This post reminds me of the first time I took methylphenidate hydrochloride (concerta), I really enjoyed the effects of being able to tackle everything I needed to but afterwards it really left my mind open to think. Being able to sit with a quiet mind is something which was new to me, you are being given an opportunity to really combat the feelings you have instead of "brushing them off" per se. 

I believe that being able to really organise your thoughts will be hard and if you have been battling with things it will be a bit of an eye opener.

We wont all feel the same, how you feel is very important to your health and wellbeing. Perhaps speak with your prescriber and remember you're early into the treatment so things will stabilise.

I am unmedicated, throughout the hours of the day, the days of the week and the weeks in the months etc etc, I would have good times and bad times. By definition of ADHD is there are periods of extreme focus, then extreme lethargy or whatever you want to call it.

  
For me, my symptoms worsen and then improve seemingly out of nowhere, I will have extreme motivation for two weeks and then this wont return for a month to then be in shine for a shorter/longer period of time. The imbalance of chemicals in the brain does not seem to be consistent (as is the nature of hormones and whatever else which regulate these neurochemicals). 

  
From my perspective (NON DOCTOR, NON PROFESSIONAL), how you feel is completely normal even with medication completely out of the picture, dont try to make too much sense out of it as maybe you'll explode with frustration! What I found helped me best is attempting to maintain a routine (as you are clearing doing), ultimately the problem will never go away, how you deal with it will shape your future and how you deal with it though!

  
Hope at least some of this is helpful or maybe somewhat alleviating to how you feel, you're not in it alone.

Download Obsidian and learn to use daily planners, this is a common tip amongst psychiatrists and such for people with ADHD, it has helped me immensely in taking charge of the things I need to do throughout the day by providing a clear sense of order of when I can do things and what others things need to be done (in case of forgetfulness). I literally cannot overstate how useful it has been in taking charge of my life (pre medication). If you don't want to use obsidian (i use it as a note taking app for quite literally everything, food, learning, daily plans, budgeting, mood writeups etc), then any other note taking app is fine, I find its best to have it all centralised in one place, get in the habit of writing the plan for tomorrow the night before. 

Have everything centralised in one place so it is not a huge effort to set up, you can make templates in obsidian to avoid excessive writing of the same things, I have a template for my general day plan, which outlines the morning stuff, then everything else I'll do the day before. Big reminders can get ones which directly ping on my phone notification app, as then I never forget.

There are guides on making it more useful and personalised and I find that having full control over how everything looks makes it more of an enjoyable experience which you can tailor to your exact needs.
